title: 2026-11-14 — A libtest name filter is a substring match

data.head: ## 2026-11-14 — A libtest name filter is a substring match

body: `cargo test -p {crate} -- {module}::tests` selects every test whose path CONTAINS that string, so a filter for `history::tests` also runs `browser_history::tests`. A gate entry that means one module either passes `--exact` with full test paths, or runs the whole crate and asserts the names it expects (`contains … ok` atoms), as the browser crate's unit entry does. A pass count read off a substring filter counts the neighbour module's tests too.

title: 2026-11-14 — A provider that needs a Dioxus runtime, read out after the rebuild

data.head: ## 2026-11-14 — A provider that needs a Dioxus runtime, read out after the rebuild

body: A provider whose construction needs a live Dioxus runtime (`Store::new_maybe_sync`, `consume_context`) can't be built in a plain `#[test]`. Build it inside a small component run by a `VirtualDom`. Have the component write what it observed into a `thread_local!`, and assert on that after `rebuild_in_place`, rather than asserting inside the component, where a failed assert is a render-time panic. The browser app's navigation-provider tests use this form. A call site that runs only inside a launched runtime (`make_doc_config`'s wiring) is still reached by no unit test, so state it as a limit.

The session gated local files in upstream's browser reference app: a remote page's favicon candidate never names a file: URL, and a navigation a non-file: document starts toward a file: URL is dropped silently, loading nothing and logging nothing.
Both refusals ride the engine's existing document_may_load predicate; a file: page keeps its file: favicon and its file: navigations, and a remote page keeps its own /favicon.ico and its https navigations.
The browser app's navigation provider gained a constructor taking the document's URL; the user's own loads (URL bar, history, home, about pages, first tab) are untouched.
The capability statement lost its two provisional, pending-the-founder clauses; its hand-written reach is otherwise unchanged.
Six browser unit tests were added (29 to 35); no engine crate, dependency, feature, log field or UI element changed, and no accessibility work was done (a11y n/a in the report's coverage).

The session closes the last gap of the file URL rule in the browser app, upstream's reference app: a remote page can no longer reach a local file through its favicon or through a navigation it starts.

The error page's document has no URL and reads as no file document.

body:
In the browser app (upstream's reference app), a page that is not a file: page can no longer reach a local file through its favicon or through a navigation it starts.
The favicon candidate is now kept only where document_may_load allows it, so a remote page names no file: favicon and never reaches the favicon probe or the shared favicon cache; a file: page's file: favicon and a remote page's own /favicon.ico are unchanged.
The navigation provider is now built for its document by a constructor, for_document. It silently drops a non-file: document's navigation to a file: URL, the way Chromium and Firefox do, loading nothing and logging nothing; the error page counts as no file: document.
Both refusals are silent: no tracing event, print, env read, log field, span, cause, exit or error was added, Cargo.lock is unchanged, and the user's own loads (URL bar, history, home, about pages, first tab) pass through no gate.
The capability statement lost its two clauses marked provisional pending the founder's choice (2 to 0), and the browser crate's unit tests went from 29 to 35. CI was green, 17 of 17 checks.
The Epoch 4 boundary batch moves the obs-plan sidecar's delegate-confirm PROVISIONAL entries to ratified on the founder's own recorded word, with no row text changed.

body:
In the browser app (upstream's reference app, a binary), a remote (non-file) page no longer names a file: URL as its favicon candidate, so no local file is probed for it and none enters the shared favicon cache; a file page's file favicon and a remote page's own /favicon.ico are unchanged.
In the browser app, the navigation provider now knows its document's URL and silently drops a non-file document's navigation to a file: URL (nothing loads, nothing is logged), as Chromium and Firefox do; every other navigation pushes to history as before.
Both refusals use the engine's existing document-may-load predicate; an absent or unparsable document URL (the error page's) reads as no file document, never a panic. The user's own loads (URL bar, history, home, about pages, first tab) pass through no gate.
The committed capability statement lost its two clauses marked provisional pending the founder's choice (2 to 0). Six browser unit tests added (29 to 35); no dependency, env read, log site, span, error or exit added; no engine crate changed.
The Epoch 4 boundary batch discharges, on the founder's word, the one master row still marked provisional (an architecture row on seeds on carriers); security-plan sidecar entries once confirmed by a delegate are worded ratified at consolidation, no security-plan row text changing for it.
